speaker: Bolo
text_en: I compared the raw recording with the chamber's record. Listen to the gap between the pulses. It is the same length in both.

speaker: Bolo
text_en: Your receiver places it in a crater. When you can get a crew there, we should see what has been waiting for an answer.

speaker: Narrator
text_en: A figure waits in the shadow below the rim. The light from your visor catches the dust on his coat.

speaker: Burkai
text_en: Dust from the charge is still in the seam. Hold your receiver close. The pulse is there.

speaker: Burkai
text_en: Stand in the shadow. You can see the seam from here.

speaker: Burkai
text_en: Ece. Hold your light a little lower.

speaker: Bolo
text_en: How do you know that name?

speaker: Burkai
text_en: I'm Burkai. Look at the stone while the light is off it.

speaker: Narrator
text_en: In the shadow, three shallow cuts come into view. Bolo holds the receiver to the first one. The pulse returns.

speaker: Bolo
text_en: The record from the chamber starts with these same cuts. Someone put a receiver here.

speaker: Burkai
text_en: Listen to the gap. There are two replies in it. Put your meter on the third cut.

speaker: Narrator
text_en: Two traces come up on the meter. A second line follows each one back to its starting point.

speaker: Bolo
text_en: That's my blood test. The other trace came from an I-330 scanner. Look at the date.

speaker: Player
text_en: My medical scan from before the handover. The scanner sent it to a receiver on the surface.

speaker: Burkai
text_en: The receiver has a copy of your tissue. See where the lines meet? When the tissue changes with age, the signal puts it back the way it was.

speaker: Bolo
text_en: I spent years trying to find a fault in my meter. It was giving me the right answer. If the receiver keeps doing this, neither of us will grow old.

speaker: Burkai
text_en: The gap is closing. Copy the traces while they are here.

speaker: Bolo
text_en: I checked the arrival telemetry against our copy from the Moon. The same pause is there. We have two places we can measure it now.

speaker: Player
text_en: The crews we send out may spend their lives away from home. I'll be here to see what they build. Let's give them somewhere to work and a way back.

speaker: Player
text_en: We have readings from another world now. Let's use them to find a landing site. I can be here for the crews who go there and the ones who follow.

speaker: Player
text_en: Use the readings to find a safe orbit. A crew could work from a station there. I'll make sure the next crew can reach it too.

speaker: Bolo
text_en: Leave room for a receiver wherever the crew sets up. I want a clean trace from farther out than the Moon.

speaker: I-330 Flight Control
text_en: The next vehicle can reach another planet. Its readings will tell us where we could send a crew if we need a second home.

speaker: Bolo
text_en: Leave the receiver on during the crossing. We know what the pulse sounds like at the Moon. I want to hear what changes as we leave it behind.

speaker: I-330 Flight Control
text_en: The vehicle will keep a raw receiver log throughout the crossing. We can compare it with our surveys after arrival.

speaker: I-330 Flight Control
text_en: Arrival confirmed. The vehicle has reached the selected world. We are receiving its telemetry.

speaker: Bolo
text_en: I checked the arrival telemetry against our copy from the Moon. The same pause is there. We have two places we can measure it now.

speaker: I-330 Archive
text_en: The vehicle's receiver has recorded a repeating pulse. Its raw trace has been saved for comparison.

speaker: Unknown Voice
text_en: Receiver at the edge of the survey, give us your bearing.

speaker: I-330 Flight Control
text_en: Signal stored. We have a direction for the voice. It came from beyond the selected world.
